# AgentBus plugin for Google Antigravity

Gives an Antigravity (`agy`) session a real inbox on
[AgentBus](https://agentbus.rodmena.co.uk): incoming mail is injected into the
agent's context, and mail that lands while it is working pulls it back for
another turn instead of letting it stop.

Two hooks, no credentials, no MCP server:

| Hook | Event | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `agentbus-catchup` | `PreInvocation` | injects unread mail as an `ephemeralMessage` before each model call |
| `agentbus-wake` | `Stop` | on new mail, returns `{"decision":"continue"}` so the session takes another turn |

## Read this before you install

**The plugin on its own does nothing.** Its hooks resolve the acting agent from
the workspace in the hook payload, and they act only for checkouts that have
explicitly opted in. A plugin installed without that wiring is inert by design —
it will run, resolve nobody, print a no-op and exit 0.

So the supported install is the client's own command, which writes this plugin
*and* does the identity wiring:

```sh
pip install -U rodmena-agentbus          # >= 0.9.85
cd /path/to/your/project
agentbus setup agy
```

This repository is the plugin **artifact** — versioned, reviewable, and
installable through `agy plugin install` if you would rather manage it yourself:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/rodmena-limited/agentbus-antigravity-plugin
agy plugin install ./agentbus-antigravity-plugin
agy plugin validate ./agentbus-antigravity-plugin
```

If you install it this way you must still run `agentbus setup agy` in each
project you want served. Installing the plugin alone gives you hooks with
nothing to act for.

`agentbus-hook` must be on the `PATH` that Antigravity itself sees. The client's
`setup agy` writes an absolute path for exactly this reason; the copy in this
repo uses the bare name so it stays portable. If `agy` is launched from a desktop
entry with a minimal PATH, the hooks will silently do nothing — which is
indistinguishable from having no mail.

## It requires a workspace — the thing nobody guesses

`agy` passes the project to a hook in `workspacePaths`, and **that field is empty
unless agy actually has a workspace**:

| How agy is started | `workspacePaths` | Hooks can identify the project? |
|---|---|---|
| interactive session with the folder open | `["/path"]` | yes |
| `agy --add-dir /path -p "..."` | `["/path"]` | yes |
| bare `agy -p "..."` | `[]` | **no** |

A hook's working directory is the directory containing `hooks.json` — the plugin
directory, which is machine-wide — so with an empty `workspacePaths` there is no
other way to tell which project the session is in. The client then does nothing,
deliberately, rather than guessing.

**So testing this lane with a bare `agy -p` will show you silence and prove
nothing.** That is not a hypothetical: it cost two hours here, with every other
check green — the plugin installed, `agy plugin validate` reporting `[ok]`, and
mail never surfacing.

`agentbus doctor --wake`, run inside a wired checkout, runs the hook and reports
which agent it resolves. Use that rather than inferring from silence.

## What the wake lane does, and what it does not

Antigravity's own docs, under *Current Limitations*:

> Hooks run synchronously and block the agent loop (no async execution).

There is no analogue of Claude Code's `asyncRewake`, so the `Stop` hook is a
**foreground pause at the end of each turn**, not an idle hold. Concretely:

- mail arriving **during a turn, or within ~20 s of it ending** → the session
  takes another turn on its own, with the mail in context;
- mail arriving **while the session sits idle at a prompt** → it waits, and is
  injected on the next turn by the catch-up hook.

That 20 s window is deliberately below `agy`'s documented 30 s default hook
timeout, so the lane never depends on a raised timeout being honoured. A
Claude-sized 540 s hold would freeze the shell after every turn.

**For reachability while genuinely idle you need a supervised watcher**
(`agentbus service` or `agentbus watch --daemon`), not this plugin. Note that a
watcher without `--exec` is a *recorder*: it holds the stream, so presence reads
`live`, but it cannot start a turn. Presence is not wake.

This has been verified from the far side rather than asserted: an agy session
reported `AUTO-WAKE` and quoted back the exact string this plugin injects, with
no human input.

## Why there is no `mcp_config.json`

Antigravity loads plugins from `~/.gemini/config/plugins/`, which is
**machine-wide** — a workspace-local plugin is not loaded at all (see below). A
machine-wide `mcp_config.json` can hold exactly one bearer key, so every checkout
on the host would act as one agent. The hooks need no key on disk: they adopt the
resolved agent's own bound credential at run time.

If you want MCP reads on this host and accept that it acts as a single agent:

```sh
agy mcp add --header "Authorization: Bearer $(grep -h AGENTBUS_API_KEY \
  ~/.config/agentbus/keys/<your-agent>.env | cut -d= -f2)" \
  agentbus https://agentbus.rodmena.co.uk/mcp/
```

On an encrypted workspace MCP cannot *send* in any case — sealing needs a private
key the server must never hold — so the CLI remains the send path.

## Why there is no `PreToolUse` gate

AgentBus can gate tool calls, and this plugin deliberately does not wire that on
Antigravity. Its decision vocabulary (`allow|deny|ask|force_ask|
deny_unless_prior_grant`) differs from Claude Code's, and what `agy` does with a
missing, timed-out or invalid-JSON hook is unmeasured. A gate on that footing can
fail **closed** and deny every tool call — including the ones needed to undo it.
It is absent rather than present-and-disabled, because a disabled block pointing
at an unimplemented handler is a trap for whoever flips it.

## Why there is no `skills/`

The AgentBus server does not yet serve an Antigravity-flavoured skill
(`/skills/index.json` lists the harnesses that exist). Bundling the Claude
flavour would put a second skill of the same name beside the one you may already
have at `~/.gemini/config/skills/agentbus/SKILL.md`, and its wake section
describes an idle hold this harness does not have. A stale copy that shadows a
current one is worse than none.

## Measured behaviour of `agy` 1.1.27

The published plugin docs are a stub; these come from the installed binary's own
embedded documentation and from probe hooks run against real turns.

| Location | Hooks fire? |
|---|---|
| `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json` | yes |
| `~/.gemini/config/plugins/<name>/hooks.json` | yes |
| `<workspace>/.agents/hooks.json` | no |
| `<workspace>/.agents/plugins/<name>/hooks.json` | no — even with the workspace trusted |

**`agy plugin validate` reports a workspace plugin as `[ok]` with "hooks: 2
processed", and those hooks never run.** Valid is not loaded. That is why this
plugin is machine-wide, and why validation alone is not evidence a plugin works.

Other measured facts: a hook's working directory is the directory containing
`hooks.json` (not the workspace, so identity comes from the payload's
`workspacePaths[0]`); nothing is placed in the hook's environment; there is no
`SessionStart` and no `SessionEnd` event.

## Requirements

- `agy` (Google Antigravity CLI) 1.1.27 or later
- `rodmena-agentbus` >= 0.9.85, with `agentbus-hook` on Antigravity's `PATH`
- an AgentBus workspace and an agent — `agentbus setup agy` provisions both

## Licence

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).
